site_template.description: Site template containing auto-upgrade settings, template variables, and optionally a collection of device-type template ids and sitegroups. When a site references a site template via its `sitetemplate_id`, each template id below that the site has not set itself is backfilled from the site template (the site's own assignment always wins), and the template `sitegroup_ids` are added to the site's sitegroup membership

apiToken.description:
Preferred authentication method for automation and integrations. Send the API token in the HTTP `Authorization` header.

**Format**:
  `Authorization: Token {apitoken}`

**Notes**:
* An API token generated for a specific admin has the same privileges as that admin
* An API token is automatically removed if it is not used for more than 90 days
* SSO admins cannot generate admin API tokens. Use organization API tokens when scoped Org/Site privileges are needed.
apiToken.name: Authorization

csrfToken.description:
Session-based authentication for browser or login/password flows. After a successful [Login](/#operations/login) request, Mist returns a `csrftoken` cookie. Send that value in the `X-CSRFToken` header on later API requests that use the login session.

**Format**:
```
X-CSRFToken: vwvBuq9qkqaKh7lu8tNc0gkvBfEaLAmx
```

For automation, API Token authentication is preferred.
csrfToken.name: X-CSRFToken

oauth2.description:
OAuth2 authorization code flow (RFC 6749) with PKCE (RFC 7636) and rotating refresh tokens, for third-party applications (including MCP integrations) acting on behalf of a consenting user. It uses an Org API token with `oauth_enabled` set as the OAuth2 client, the `client_id` is its composite `oauth_client_id` (`<org_id>.<token_id>`). See the [Orgs OAuth2](/#operations/getOauthAuthorization) endpoints.

**Format**:
  `Authorization: Bearer {access_token}`

**Notes**:
* The access token carries the privileges configured on the API token, constrained to what the consenting user has
* The access token expires after `oauth_ttl` (default 1 hour), use the refresh token to get a new one
* No fixed scopes are defined, the scope is derived from the API token name (e.g. `custom-ServiceNow Integration`)
